A.explanation: Sound is longitudinal, but the period is not 25 ms. Repeating points such as upward zero-crossings at 5 ms and 25 ms are 20 ms apart.

B.explanation: Sound is a longitudinal wave and $T = 20 \text{ ms}$ gives $f = 1/T = 50 \text{ Hz}$.

walkthrough: Recall the wave type: a sound wave is a longitudinal wave because air particles oscillate parallel to the direction of energy propagation. The graph shape does not change this.
Read the displacement-time graph to find the period $T$. The trace crosses zero going upward at $5 \text{ ms}$, again at $25 \text{ ms}$ and again at $45 \text{ ms}$.
Calculate one repeat interval: $T = 25 \text{ ms} - 5 \text{ ms} = 20 \text{ ms} = 20 \times 10^{-3} \text{ s}$.

Use $f = 1/T$ to get frequency: $f = 1/(20 \times 10^{-3} \text{ s}) = 50 \text{ Hz}$. The amplitude $3 \text{ } \mu\text{m}$ is the maximum displacement, but the transverse descriptions are wrong and wavelength cannot have unit $\text{ms}$.
